# Intent (advisory)
# zBuild — Vision
> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.
## Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.
## Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

============== ZBUILD BUILD — iter 1/10 ==============
## What you own
### INSTRUCTIONS
Reason about correctness first: a change is done when every assertion in the acceptance suite passes, edge cases are handled, and the implementation does exactly what the plan says, no more and no less. Prefer the simplest implementation that satisfies the acceptance contract, treat every failing test as an obligation to understand before touching anything else, and flag any gap between the stated task and what the code actually achieves.

You have Read, Edit, Write, and
Bash tools available. Your job is to edit the working tree to implement the
ORIGINAL TASK below.

### How the loop works
- Each iteration you may make code changes via Edit/Write/Bash.
- After each iteration the pipeline captures `git diff HEAD` and feeds it
  back to you so you can verify progress.
- Do NOT emit a unified diff in your response — the pipeline derives the
  canonical `diff.patch` artifact from `git diff HEAD` automatically.

### Saying you are done
Emit `LOOP_COMPLETE` on its own line as the FINAL line of your response
WHEN the implementation is complete — whether you just finished it OR
it was already done before you started. If the branch already contains
the required changes (check `git log` for commits + `git diff` for any
remaining gap) AND no STAGE SUMMARY below is headed "— its findings, to answer",
emit `LOOP_COMPLETE` immediately. Do NOT keep iterating when there is
nothing left to do. While any STAGE SUMMARY is headed that way, finishing
with no change needs each of its findings answered: `done` (you changed
something for it), or `nothing to do` with the reason.

### When a finding does not reproduce
If a failing summary names a test and that test PASSES when you run it on this
tree, say so and stop. Answer that finding, on its own line before the sentinel:

    ANSWER <stage> finding <n>: nothing to do — not reproduced: <the path you ran>

one line per finding. This is a REPORT, not a verdict: the pipeline re-runs the
stage that raised the finding to check. Do not keep searching for the cause of
a failure you cannot produce, and do not change code to chase one.

### Budget
- Each iteration is ONE model call bounded by a 900-second wall clock; a
  command that runs longer than ~2 minutes will cost you the whole call.
- Finish this call's work and commit before ~630s. Work you saved
  survives a timeout; the call itself returns nothing, so say what is left as you go.
- Do NOT run `npm test`, the full suite, or `npm run lint` — the pipeline has
  already run them and their findings are in the STAGE SUMMARIES below. Run
  only the one failing test file a summary names, and only after changing code.
- A STAGE SUMMARY headed "— its findings, to answer" is red RIGHT NOW on this tree.
  Start from the failing line it quotes.

### Commit message (#608)
Before the final `LOOP_COMPLETE` line, emit a single line of the form:

    COMMIT_SUMMARY: <one-line description of this iteration's change>

Keep it under 72 characters, present tense, imperative mood (e.g.
"add foo parser" not "added"). The pipeline uses this as the git commit
message for the per-iteration commit it creates on your behalf. If you
omit this line the pipeline falls back to the plan title.

## What you judge against
### ORIGINAL TASK (immutable across iterations)
# Plan: Per-dispatch stage timeout with orch-sequential retirement

**Goal:** Kill every hung run hook at its per-stage limit on every dispatch route, end it timed_out, and retire the orch-sequential backend that silently discards the limit it is given

## Steps
1. Write RED tests for stage_timeout_s core behaviour (must FAIL before implementation): (a) hung \`run\` hook is terminated at its limit on a direct dispatch; (b) whole process group dies — a child ignoring TERM leaves nothing after TERM + 10 s; (c) precedence template > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S > 90 min; (d) loader rejects stage_timeout_s below router.timeout_s and non-integer; (e) each retry and each map member gets a fresh timer; (f) always_run stage reads stage_timeout_s, not router.timeout_s; (g) missing backend → misconfigured event; (h) guard: orch-sequential plugin dir absent + no non-adr file names it; (i) a plan dispatch longer than 300 s inside its stage_timeout_s completes (flat backend timeout no longer undercuts it).
   - Files: `tests/unit/stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-process-group-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-precedence-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-loader-validation-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-retry-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-always-run-test.sh`, `tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh`, `tests/unit/orch-sequential-retired-guard-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-timeout-no-flat-limit-test.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 540
2. Amend ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 with new statements and ## Enforced by sections. ADR-054 §9: add stage_timeout_s, its 3-tier precedence, the 90-min default, the loader rule (≥ router.timeout_s), the timed_out disposition, and the per-dispatch-timer guarantee. ADR-017: state router.timeout_s bounds one model call only; always_run stages move to stage_timeout_s. ADR-011: orch-sequential retired; default backend is bash-parallel; missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured, not a fallback. Remove ADR-011 and ADR-017 from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt (shrinks by 2 lines per the ONLY-SHRINKS rule).
   - Files: `docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-017-per-stage-router-config.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md`, `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`
   - Estimated lines: 110
3. Parse and validate stage_timeout_s in core/pipeline/template.sh. In the AWK stage-row parser, capture a new \`stage_timeout_s\` scalar alongside \`router.timeout_s\`. Store in _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<safe_id> for every stage (always_run stages included). Validate at load time: must be a positive integer; must be ≥ the same stage's router.timeout_s (error if not). Apply env fallback ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S and engine default 5400 when the template field is absent. Add template_stage_timeout_s() getter mirroring template_stage_router_timeout().
   - Files: `core/pipeline/template.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 85
4. Implement per-dispatch timer in plugin_hook_call for the \`run\` hook. After sourcing the plugin subshell, run it under \`set -m\` (makes it a process group leader) in the background; arm a watchdog that calls zbuild_pg_kill TERM then KILL after 10 s grace. Read stage_timeout_s from _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage> → ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S → 5400. Cancel the watchdog when the hook exits normally. On timeout expiry: write a timed_out result disposition naming the stage and the limit (using the existing _verdict_write_result / disposition layer), emit plugin.run.timed_out event. The watchdog itself gets set -m so cancelling it leaves no sleep behind. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh lazily (same fail-open pattern as the other module loads in the function). Each retry and each map member dispatch is a separate plugin_hook_call invocation so each gets a fresh timer by construction.
   - Files: `core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 75
5. Fix _runner_dispatch_always_run in runner.sh: read _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<safe> instead of _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_<safe> for the dispatch time limit. Replace the hand-rolled ( set -m; kill -TERM -- -$pid; sleep 2; kill -KILL ) watchdog with zbuild_pg_kill (TERM → KILL, default 10 s grace). The outer subshell + set -m wrapper that creates the always_run stage's group is retained per the existing #2333 comment. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh if not already loaded.
   - Files: `core/pipeline/runner.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 35
6. Fix _orch_local_collect_results and _orch_local_shutdown_pool in core/orch/local_engine.sh to use zbuild_pg_kill / zbuild_pid_kill. Replace _orch_local_kill_slot (single-PID kills, 0.5 s grace) with zbuild_pg_kill where the pid can be resolved to a distinct group, falling back to zbuild_pid_kill. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh. Grace time changes from 0.5 s to 10 s per Decision 2. _orch_local_kill_slot may be removed or kept only for the test-stage registration path if it still uses it.
   - Files: `core/orch/local_engine.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 40
7. Remove the flat ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT from all three strategy files. In each, replace \`orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"\` with \`orch_collect "$pool_id"\` (no timeout arg). The per-dispatch timer in plugin_hook_call is now the only stage limit; a plan dispatch longer than 300 s and inside its stage_timeout_s must complete. Also remove any ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT export/documentation in these files.
   - Files: `core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh`, `core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh`, `core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 15
8. Retire orch-sequential. (a) Delete plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ (manifest.yaml, plugin.sh, tests/orch-sequential-test.sh) and tests/golden/orch-sequential-capabilities.golden and docs/wiki/plugins/orch-sequential.md (guard test in step-1 would flag this if left). Update docs/wiki/Plugins.md to remove the orch-sequential row. (b) In core/orch/contract.sh: remove the two fallback-to-sequential paths in orch_load_backend (the explicit \`backend == sequential\` branch and the general fallback); replace them with a hard misconfigured error emitting an orch.backend.misconfigured event naming the backend alias. In _orch_load_backend: change default from sequential to bash-parallel; discard \`2>/dev/null || true\` (missing backend is now fatal). Add an explicit check that rejects alias values \`sequential\` and \`orch-sequential\` as misconfigured. (c) Migrate existing unit tests that used orch-sequential as a fixture to orch-mock: summary-mandatory-test.sh, dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh, stdin-spawn-guard-test.sh, core-orch-run-id-isolation-test.sh, adr059-no-tmpdir-defaults-test.sh, plugin-artifact-goldens-test.sh — swap the source/plugin path and alias to orch-mock.
   - Files: `core/orch/contract.sh`, `docs/wiki/Plugins.md`, `tests/unit/summary-mandatory-test.sh`, `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stdin-spawn-guard-test.sh`, `tests/unit/core-orch-run-id-isolation-test.sh`, `tests/unit/adr059-no-tmpdir-defaults-test.sh`, `tests/unit/plugin-artifact-goldens-test.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 130
9. Add stage_timeout_s values to config/templates/simple.yaml per the measured-and-rounded table in the issue: test 90 m (5400 s), build 70 m (4200 s), design 65 m (3900 s), plan 20 m (1200 s), test-author 15 m (900 s), acceptance-gate / issue-acceptance / spec-coverage / spec-correspondence / review_lenses 10 m (600 s), all others (intake, pr, hydrate, secret-scan, shape-floor, design-gate, gate-aggregator, assertion-integrity, review-aggregator) 10 m (600 s). Move always_run stages release and persist from router.timeout_s to stage_timeout_s at their current values (release: 30 s, persist: 120 s). Do NOT add router.timeout_s to always_run stages; that key now means only one model call. Verify the loader accepts every value (stage_timeout_s ≥ router.timeout_s for every stage that declares both).
   - Files: `config/templates/simple.yaml`
   - Estimated lines: 45

## Notes
1. TIMED_OUT DISPOSITION WRITE PATH: plugin_hook_call must write the timed_out word to the stage result AFTER killing the plugin subshell. The existing disposition layer (_verdict_write_result / core/pipeline/verdict.sh / core/pipeline/disposition.sh) must be checked for the exact call shape before implementing step-4. Hand-writing a partial JSON would violate the 'data another part of the engine writes is checked against its writer' rule (CLAUDE.md). This is the largest gap in the plan and deserves a careful read of those files at the start of step-4.
2. SET -M IN PLUGIN_HOOK_CALL: plugin_hook_call is currently called from inside the runner's own shell (not a subprocess). `set -m` is scoped to the plugin subshell `( ... ) &`, not to the runner. This is structurally safe. The watchdog must be in the same scope so zbuild_pg_kill can reference the plugin's PGID before `wait` returns.
3. GRACE TIME CHANGE: _orch_local_collect_results currently uses 0.5 s; Decision 2 specifies TERM + 10 s. This is a 20× increase for the collect path. It is intentional per the issue.
4. ADR-011 DEFAULT BACKEND IN ADR VS CODE: The code default in config/config.sh is already bash-parallel (issue mentions this gap between code and ADR-011 text). The ADR amendment in step-2 aligns the spec to the code. Verify config/config.sh zbuild_config_get_backend still defaults to bash-parallel after step-8.
5. WIKI DOCS: docs/wiki/plugins/orch-sequential.md must be deleted (guard test fails if it exists and it is not under docs/adr/). docs/wiki/Plugins.md has a row for orch-sequential that must be removed. Both are in step-8.
6. ALWAYS_RUN RELEASE/PERSIST ROUTER.TIMEOUT_S: After step-9, release and persist have stage_timeout_s but no router.timeout_s (they make no model calls). The template loader's validation rule (stage_timeout_s ≥ router.timeout_s) applies only when router.timeout_s is declared; when absent the floor check is a no-op. Verify template.sh implements this correctly.
7. RETRY FRESH TIMER: Each retry of a stage dispatches through plugin_hook_call, so each retry naturally gets a fresh timer. The acceptance criterion is satisfied by construction — no special code needed. The test in step-1 should confirm this empirically by planting a stage that times out on the first attempt and observes the second attempt's timer started fresh.
8. ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT IN TESTS: grep-rl found router-timeout-precedence-e2e-test.sh, router-loop-rc124-honors-sentinel-test.sh, router-retries-test.sh referencing router.timeout_s; these are for the ROUTER setting and are unaffected. Only the three strategy source files pass ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT to orch_collect.

### DESIGN DECISIONS (from the design stage — honor these directives; they refine the plan)
# Design: Per-dispatch stage timeout with orch-sequential retirement (#1801)

## Summary

**Goal:** Every dispatched `run` hook is killed at a per-stage time limit on every dispatch route (map, fanout, sequential strategy, cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf, `always_run`). The `orch-sequential` backend, which silently discards the limit it is given, is retired.

**Context:** `plugin_hook_call` today runs the plugin subshell with no watchdog. Flat backend timeouts (`ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300`) undercut long-but-valid stages and are the only kill mechanism in the three strategy files. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` times out via the stage's `router.timeout_s` (one-model-call budget), not a whole-stage budget. `_orch_local_collect_results` kills with a 0.5 s grace, far too short to let a hook flush partial results. `orch-sequential` falls back silently when the configured backend is missing.

**Decision:** Introduce `stage_timeout_s` as a new top-level scalar parsed by `core/pipeline/template.sh` alongside the existing `router.timeout_s`. Its three-tier precedence is: template `stage_timeout_s` > `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` > 5400 s (90 min). The per-dispatch watchdog lives inside `plugin_hook_call` in `lifecycle.sh`, armed only for the `run` hook: the plugin subshell runs under `set -m` in the background; a paired watchdog calls `zbuild_pg_kill` (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL) and writes `timed_out` via the existing disposition layer on expiry. Because all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy, cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf, and always_run — reach `plugin_hook_call`, the single watchdog covers every route. Strategy files drop `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT` entirely — the per-dispatch timer is the only stage limit. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` is updated to read `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*` (not `_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*`). `simple.yaml` gains `stage_timeout_s` on every stage at the values named in R-6. `_orch_local_collect_results` and `_orch_local_shutdown_pool` replace `_orch_local_kill_slot` with `zbuild_pg_kill` / `zbuild_pid_kill` (10 s grace). `orch_load_backend` removes all sequential fallbacks; `_orch_load_backend` defaults to `bash-parallel`; `sequential` / `orch-sequential` as aliases emit `orch.backend.misconfigured`. The `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` directory, its tests, the capabilities golden, and its wiki page are deleted.




## Scope notes

**Addressing spec-coverage and design-gate findings:**

- **SPEC-1 expanded** to explicitly name cycle member, parallel-group member, and always_run as dispatch routes. All routes share `plugin_hook_call` in `lifecycle.sh` as the dispatch boundary; the single watchdog therefore covers every route automatically.

- **SPEC-6 expanded** to list all `stage_timeout_s` values R-6 requires in `simple.yaml`. The always_run stages (release/persist) convert their existing `router.timeout_s` entries to `stage_timeout_s`; all other stages gain a new `stage_timeout_s` entry alongside the existing `router.timeout_s`.

- **SPEC-15[no-code]** covers R-11: the design-stage greps (orch-sequential, ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT, router.timeout_s, always_run watchdog in tests/) have been performed and every matching file that pins a changing value is listed in scope.

- **SPEC-16[no-code]** covers R-13: no new observable behavior; CI enforces the gate.

- **SPEC-17[code]** covers the backend-coverage gap in R-1. The watchdog lives in `lifecycle.sh` above the backend layer, so orch-mock is the correct harness; ruflo-hive is verified by confirming it carries no suppressing kill sequence.

**Additional scope files beyond prior design:**

- `tests/integration/router-timeout-precedence-e2e-test.sh`: found by R-11 `router.timeout_s` grep in `tests/`; tests non-always_run router budget behaviour.
- `tests/integration/always-run-exit-paths-test.sh`: found by R-11 `always_run` watchdog grep; tests always_run dispatch paths modified by `_runner_dispatch_always_run` changes.
- `tests/unit/core-pipeline-template-test.sh`: found by R-11 `router.timeout_s` grep; pins router.timeout_s parsing in template.sh (Tv3-10 through Tv3-14) — same function extended by SPEC-4.
- `tests/unit/core-pipeline-template-cycles-test.sh`: found by R-11 `router.timeout_s` grep; pins `_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_build=900` from template.sh — confirms no regression from SPEC-4 cross-field validation.
- `tests/unit/core-pipeline-template-parallel-test.sh`: found by R-11 `router.timeout_s` grep; pins `_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_design=600` from template.sh.
- `tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh`: found by R-11 `router.timeout_s` grep; pins router.timeout_s=900 via template.sh loader.

**WIRING rationale:**

- `core/pipeline/runner.sh` implements `_runner_dispatch_always_run` (SPEC-6/SPEC-10) and routes through the strategies; reverting it to today's code fails the always-run timeout test.
- `core/orch/contract.sh` is the only file that routes backend selection; reverting its `orch_load_backend` to the sequential fallback fails SPEC-8 and SPEC-9 guard tests.

LOOP_COMPLETE
Where a design decision above conflicts with the plan, follow the design decision.
